results.title: How to Live Stream on YouTube Shorts | Upstream.so
results.content:
### Build a real 9:16 output

In OBS, open Settings → Video and set Base (Canvas) Resolution and Output (Scaled) Resolution to a portrait size. A practical starting point is 1080 × 1920; 720 × 1280 is a lighter alternative. Keep the output portrait rather than placing a vertical video inside a landscape canvas.

Then rearrange your sources to fit. A wide gameplay capture may need a carefully chosen crop; a tutorial may work better with the demonstration above a camera view. Do not stretch a landscape image until people and objects look unnaturally thin. [...] ## Can live streams appear on the YouTube Shorts Feed?

Yes. “Going live on Shorts” means broadcasting a vertical YouTube live stream that viewers can find while scrolling Shorts. It is still a simple live broadcast, not a short-form video upload. Viewers can enter a full-screen live experience and move between live streams.

There are important exceptions: Tablets, and Scheduled streams.

The tablet app does not show live streams in the shorts feed, ever.

Scheduled live streams and Premieres do not appear in the vertical live feed either.

If Shorts-feed discovery is your goal, use the immediate Go live workflow described below rather than assuming an event scheduled in advance will qualify. See YouTube’s vertical live feed guidance. [...] No: it is a live broadcast, not a Shorts upload. Plan duration and replay handling separately. See YouTube’s live streaming limits before setting up a long-running program.

### Can I run prerecorded content as a vertical live stream?

Upstream supports that workflow through uploaded content and vertical cloud playout. Make the program worth watching, describe replays honestly, and ensure you have the necessary rights. Treat continuous streaming as a programming choice, not a guarantee of growth or monetization.

## Start with one useful vertical broadcast

For a live conversation, use your phone. For a produced real-time show, use OBS. For an ongoing program built from existing videos, use Upstream.
